title: Ethanol plant worker caught with bomb files, batteries, map in plot that could have killed thousands: feds
summary: Andrew Kozak stays jailed until trial after prosecutors said bomb-making files and a map of the BioUrja Renewables plant were found on his hard drive.
story: Following the discovery of a credible explosive device in Peoria, FBI Special Agent in Charge Ryan Presley praises the swift coordination between the FBI, Peoria Police Department, and the ATF. Presley highlights the quick capture of a suspect and reminds the public that community vigilance and reporting suspicious behavior remain vital to defending the homeland.

An Illinois ethanol plant worker accused of emailing a bomb threat to his workplace will remain behind bars until trial after federal authorities revealed investigators found bomb-making files and a map of the facility during searches of his property.

Judge Ronald L. Hanna ordered Andrew M. Kozak, of Chillicothe, held without bond Friday. Hanna warned that the explosive found at BioUrja Renewables was a working device that could have killed people and caused major damage, 25News reported.

Rather than following a single timeline, prosecutors used two slide presentations in court to connect the physical items seized from Kozak's home and vehicle to the digital trail behind the Nov. 13 scare – which forced roughly 2,500 homes and businesses within a one-mile radius across Peoria and East Peoria to evacuate for nearly 24 hours, court records and 25News show.
IOWA RESIDENTS NEAR AMMUNITION PLANT TOLD TO VACATE BEFORE ARMY DETONATES 5 TONS OF BOMB-MAKING CHEMICALS
During a Nov. 16 search of Kozak's home, FBI agents recovered AA rechargeable batteries, copper sheeting, wiring and white tape, prosecutors told the court.
Andrew Kozak is facing federal charges in the Illinois bomb scare. (Courtesy Peoria Police Department)
The supplies matched components from a partially damaged device found near a tank at the plant, which contained a powdery substance and used timers or remote-control parts.
MISSOURI MAN’S EXPLOSIVES TUTORIAL HELPED NEW ORLEANS TERRORIST PLAN NYE ATTACK, FEDS SAY
Agents also found a laptop missing its hard drive, later recovering the drive inside Kozak's vehicle alongside a map of the BioUrja facility, prosecutors said.
Files stored on that drive covered shaped-charge explosives, a blasting cap well and a video about copper-based explosives, prosecutors told the court.
ARIZONA MAN ARRESTED AFTER ALLEGEDLY EMAILING WHITE HOUSE BOMB THREAT TO TUCSON NEWS STATION
Investigators also found internet searches for videos of ethanol tank blasts and a 2023 investigation into an industrial ethanol plant explosion.

According to 25News, prosecutors tied Kozak to the warning email sent to BioUrja employees — which carried the subject line "severe site security risk" and claimed multiple bombs were hidden inside — using security footage and internet records from the morning of Nov. 13.
Andrew Kozak is the BioUrja Renewables employee accused in connection with an explosive device found at the company's Peoria, Illinois, ethanol plant. (Andrew Kozak/LinkedIn)
FBI NABS SUSPECT ACCUSED OF SENDING HUNDREDS OF WHITE POWDER LETTERS TO PUBLIC OFFICIALS: SOURCE

Cameras captured Kozak arriving at a Peoria grocery store just before 9:45 a.m., prosecutors said. Nearly 15 minutes later, someone on the store's public Wi-Fi set up an email account under the name "Jake Armitage" — an alias Kozak's wife reportedly told FBI agents he had previously used on Facebook.

The threat went out at 10:16 a.m., two minutes before cameras showed Kozak walking inside the store wearing a sweatshirt from an old job. A license plate camera captured his vehicle leaving the lot after he checked out at 10:31 a.m.
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X
Investigators also traced activity on the email account back to an internet address at Kozak's Chillicothe home, prosecutors said.

Bill Daly, a former FBI investigator and international security expert who worked on the 1993 World Trade Center bombing, told Fox News Digital that the case stands out because bombers trying to cause mass casualties rarely warn targets ahead of time.

The BioUrja Renewables ethanol plant in Peoria, Illinois, where authorities discovered an explosive device, prompting a one-mile evacuation and a federal investigation. (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect)

"Normally they wouldn't be calling in a bomb threat," Daly said, noting that investigators will examine whether the sender was trying to "be kind of the hero of the day" by pointing out security gaps or whether another workplace grievance was behind the scare.
SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

Kozak's public defenders argued in court that the batteries, tape and wiring were ordinary household items and stressed that prosecutors had not proved he built or planted the device, noting he is only charged with making threats, 25News reported. Fox News Digital reached out to the Federal Public Defender's Office for comment on the matter.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM THE FOX TRUE CRIME HUB

Addressing the absence of bomb-making or planting charges in the initial indictment, Daly said federal prosecutors often move quickly with threat counts to keep a suspect in custody while forensic and chemical testing continues.
SEND US A TIP

"They had enough to present for the indictment, and as they get more of the information, it gives them time to pull together more of the evidence," Daly said. "It doesn't mean that what he's currently charged with may be the only charges — those charges can change and be updated as more information becomes available."
ILLINOIS MAN ACCUSED OF THREATENING CONGRESS WITH WHITE SUBSTANCES IN LETTERS MARKED WITH HIS RETURN ADDRESS
Federal investigators swarmed the facility where there was a bomb scare at a sprawling Illinois ethanol plant that spans 44½ football fields. (FBI Springfield Office)
GOT A TIP?
Hanna ruled that Kozak was both a danger to the public and a flight risk, pointing to his criminal record and noting his family had left the area.
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

Kozak, who had worked at BioUrja for about 10 months before being arrested when he showed up for work Nov. 16, pleaded not guilty on Nov. 17 to federal charges of making bomb threats and sending a threat across state lines.

He has a two-decade criminal history in Nebraska that includes burglary-related convictions across four counties and two stints in state prison between 2008 and 2014, court and corrections records reviewed by Fox News Digital show.

A pretrial hearing is set for Dec. 3 before U.S. District Judge Jonathan E. Hawley, court records show.

title: California man accused of making online threats against ICE agents: DOJ
summary: A California man was arrested after allegedly making social media threats against ICE agents and advocating for armed attacks on government facilities.
story: Federal authorities have arrested a 37-year-old California man accused of threatening violence against ICE officers and plotting an armed attack on a detention facility.
A California man was arrested after allegedly making social media threats against Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents, the Department of Justice announced on Monday.
Leonard Michael Fierro, 37, of Hacienda Heights, is facing one count of interstate threats.

Fierro used social media to threaten violence against ICE agents, advocate armed attacks on government facilities and encourage others to participate in a violent revolution against the U.S. government, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Central District of California.

"Threats of violence against federal law enforcement officers is not protected speech. They are serious criminal acts that endanger public safety and undermine the rule of law," U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli said in a statement.
FLORIDA ATTORNEY ACCUSED OF THREATENING TO SHOOT ICE AGENTS WHILE TRYING TO BUY GUN
Leonard Michael Fierro, 37, of Hacienda Heights, is facing one count of interstate threats. (Bloomberg via Getty Images)
"We will aggressively prosecute those who seek to intimidate, harm, or incite violence against the men and women who enforce our nation's laws," he continued.

Last month, the FBI became aware of threatening posts allegedly made by Fierro on Instagram. In multiple posts and stories, Fierro allegedly called for an armed uprising against the U.S. government, advocated for violence against federal agents and encouraged others to join him in conducting attacks against ICE facilities.
In one post, he allegedly asked followers to meet outside ICE facilities, the White House and other government buildings to "take up arms" and "overthrow" the government.
Fierro also allegedly called for an armed mob to storm the Adelanto ICE Processing Center, break migrant detainees free and violently overthrow the government.
Investigators also discovered that Fierro owned a firearm and had purchased approximately 700 rounds of 9mm ammunition in October and early November.
Leonard Michael Fierro allegedly called for an armed mob to storm the Adelanto ICE Processing Center, break migrant detainees free and violently overthrow the government. (Getty Images)

He also made extensive online searches about tactical equipment, ballistic protection, surveillance countermeasures, bolt cutters, GPS tracking devices, government facilities and the Adelanto ICE detention facility, according to investigators.

Fierro allegedly researched specific ICE officers and searched for information regarding a leaked database of Department of Homeland Security employees. Investigators also said he had what appeared to be a planning checklist with references to tactical gear, ammunition, GPS trackers, a rental vehicle, communication equipment and other items allegedly associated with his plot.

On Nov. 5, FBI agents searched Fierro, his vehicle and his residence under judicially authorized search warrants, recovering a gun, 19 loaded magazines, more than 400 additional rounds of ammunition, tactical body armor, ballistic plates, GPS tracking devices, bolt cutters, digital devices and other equipment.

Authorities later reviewed data stored on Fierro’s devices and found several videos allegedly recorded by him in late October and early November in which he discussed initiating a violent revolution, targeting ICE agents and encouraged others to conduct armed attacks against government facilities and officials.
FBI ARRESTS PROTESTER WHO THREATENED TO KILL ICE OFFICER'S FAMILY AT NJ DETENTION CENTER PROTEST, BLANCHE SAYS
Leonard Michael Fierro would face a statutory maximum sentence of five years behind bars if convicted. (John Moore/Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Investigators also recovered what appeared to be a farewell video that included Fierro talking about his anticipated death, leaving instructions for family members and saying that he expected to be found "riddled with bullet holes."

Notes with Spanish-language phrases that appeared to have been made to communicate with migrant detainees during a planned attempt to free people held at an ICE detention facility were also found by investigators.
If convicted, Fierro would face a statutory maximum sentence of five years behind bars.
The FBI continues to investigate.

title: Coast Guard boards 2 foreign ships bound for US amid reports of Iranian hacking probe
summary: U.S. Coast Guard cyber teams boarded two foreign vessels in the Gulf of America after their networks were compromised by foreign cyber actors at sea.
story: U.S. Central Command said U.S. Marines in the Gulf of Oman "boarded M/T Celestial Sea, an Iranian-flagged commercial oil tanker suspected of attempting to violate the U.S. blockade by transiting toward an Iranian port." (Credit: CENTCOM)

The U.S. Coast Guard deployed specialized cyber teams to board two foreign-flagged commercial ships bound for U.S. ports in August after indications that their networks had been compromised by "foreign cyber actors," a Coast Guard spokesperson told Fox News Digital on Monday.
The offshore operations took place Aug. 21 and 24 in the Gulf of America, with teams mitigating the threats before the vessels reached U.S. ports.
The confirmation came as The Wall Street Journal also reported Monday that U.S. authorities are investigating whether Iran was involved in dozens of cyberattacks targeting energy tankers.
FEARS OF CHINA SPYING ON US MILITARY PROMPT GOP HAWKS TO DEMAND RETALIATION AGAINST THE SHIPPING GIANT
The U.S. Coast Guard and Homeland Security Investigations conducted a joint boarding operation aboard the tanker in the Port of Los Angeles. (Department of Homeland Security)

"The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG), in close coordination with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and federal cybersecurity experts, recently conducted joint offshore security boardings of two inbound foreign-flagged commercial vessels in the Gulf of America," a Coast Guard spokesperson said.

"The measures were designed to ensure the integrity of the vessel’s operational and information technology systems following indications that the networks of both vessels were compromised by foreign cyber actors."

The Coast Guard said a specialized team of law enforcement personnel, Coast Guard Cyber Protection Team members, a vessel inspector and FBI Cyber Action Team operators boarded the first vessel Aug. 21 to investigate the suspected cybersecurity breach.
"The captain, crew and shore-side corporate staff were critical partners in helping to ensure the threats were mitigated," the spokesperson added.
A similar multiagency boarding and safety verification operation was conducted Aug. 24 aboard the second vessel, also in the Gulf of America, the Coast Guard said.
FRENCH SUPERMARKETS FACE MILLIONS IN LOSSES AFTER CYBERATTACK HITS REFRIGERATORS NATIONWIDE
The Coast Guard has complete authority to make sure ships comply with U.S. law and international law. (iStock)
No operational disruptions, vessel instability, threats to crew safety or environmental impacts have been reported.
The Coast Guard said it is coordinating with port operators, vessel owners and local maritime stakeholders to ensure port operations continue safely and without interruption.

According to The Wall Street Journal, attackers exploited vulnerabilities in Fortinet networking equipment, prompting Coast Guard boardings after crews received bomb threats warning that "traitor ships will burn in hell."
STRAIT OF HORMUZ CRISIS TRAPS 6,000 SAILORS AS ATTACKS ON SHIPS MOUNT, UN MARITIME CHIEF SAYS
A Coast Guard MH-65 Dolphin helicopter crew. (U.S. Coast Guard photo by Chief Petty Officer David Mosley)
As many as 50 vessels carrying oil, liquefied petroleum, chemicals and other potentially explosive cargo are believed to have been targeted, the outlet reported, citing U.S. officials.
A European shipping executive also said officers received threats on their cellphones.
A ransom letter addressed to the captain of the Liberian-flagged supertanker Prosperity, which was carrying about 2.3 million barrels of oil, described the operation as a "planned execution."

Hackers reportedly breached one vessel's propulsion and navigation systems, disrupting communications for about 30 hours and forcing the crew to switch to manual procedures, potentially delaying energy shipments to Asia and Europe.
AMERICA MUST DEFEND OUR DIGITAL INFRASTRUCTURE, HERE AND OVERSEAS, TO WIN THE NEXT WAR

The U.S. Coast Guard will be ending admissions for college students wanting to commission as officers that take race into consideration as part of the Trump administration’s continued anti-diversity, equity and inclusion initiative, Fox News Digital has learned. (Justin Sullivan/Getty Images)

"The Marine Transportation System is vital to America's economic prosperity and national security, and safeguarding it against potential cyber risks is a standard part of the United States Coast Guard's safety and security mission," the Coast Guard spokesperson said.

"Just as we monitor for mechanical or weather-related hazards, we incorporate cyber risk management into our routine, professional approach to facilitating commerce and ensuring safe vessel transits into and from our ports and waterways.
"While confirmed cyber disruptions in the maritime domain remain uncommon, even isolated technical issues can cause avoidable commercial delays.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"We encourage all maritime stakeholders to leverage Coast Guard Cyber Command’s free, non-regulatory technical resources to maintain strong digital hygiene and report any suspected anomalies to the National Response Center," the spokesperson added.

Emma Bussey is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital. Before joining Fox, she worked at The Telegraph with the U.S. overnight team, across desks including foreign, politics, news, sport and culture.

title: Newly elected Florida commissioner's son shot dead inside tent during camping trip
summary: Local law enforcement is appealing for tips after a weekend camping trip along the Blackwater River ended in tragedy for a Florida official's family.
story: Carey Washington Vinson was fatally shot inside his tent along Florida's Blackwater River on Sunday night.
A newly elected Florida politician is mourning the death of his son after the young man was fatally shot inside his tent during a weekend camping trip, his father confirmed Monday.

Joe Vinson, who made history earlier this year as the first non-party-affiliated county commissioner elected in Escambia County, announced the tragedy on Instagram, revealing that his son, Carey Washington Vinson, was killed while camping with friends near the Blackwater River in the Florida Panhandle.

"I don’t know how to say this," Joe Vinson wrote. "Our son Carey Washington Vinson is dead. He was camping with friends on the Blackwater River last night when a gunshot from outside their campsite struck him in his tent."
CALIFORNIA NURSING STUDENT AND MOM ARRESTED MONTHS AFTER MAN’S BODY TURNS UP IN RAVINE: POLICE
Carey Washington Vinson was killed while camping with friends near the Blackwater River in the Florida Panhandle, his father confirmed Monday. (@joepensacola/Instagram)
He added, "It’s an ongoing investigation, and I don’t have any more details at this time. We are shocked and heartbroken about our sweet boy."
According to the Santa Rosa County Sheriff's Office, officers were dispatched to the Blackwater River area on Sunday following a 911 call about a shooting.
First responders arrived to find a male victim with a gunshot wound to the head and pronounced him dead at the scene.
RUSH HOUR ROAD RAGE SUSPECT’S BAIL REVOKED AS SLAIN UTILITY WORKER’S SUPPORTERS SHOUT AT ACCUSED MURDERER
Joe Vinson was elected this year as the first non-party-affiliated county commissioner in Escambia County history. (Escambia County)
Carey, 19, and his friends had been camping on sandbars along the river since Friday, Santa Rosa County Sheriff's Office Chief Deputy Randy Tifft told People magazine.
Law enforcement has not yet said whether they believe the shooting was intentional or accidental.
Escambia County Sheriff Chip Simmons offered condolences to the commissioner's family on Facebook.

"There are simply no words that can ease the pain of losing a child," Simmons said. "I ask that you join me in keeping Joe and his entire family in your thoughts and prayers during this incredibly difficult time. May God grant them strength, comfort, and peace in the days ahead."
LOUISIANA MAN ACCUSED OF RANDOM NATURE TRAIL MURDER, KILLING COWORKER WITH CROSSBOW DAYS LATER
Law enforcement has not yet said whether they believe the shooting was intentional or accidental. (iStock)
Detectives are urging anyone who was in the area or witnessed suspicious activity to come forward.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"This incident remains under active investigation," a spokesperson for the Santa Rosa County Sheriff's Office told Fox News Digital in an email. "We will provide updates as additional information becomes available for release."
Fox News Digital reached out to Joe Vinson for comment.

Sophia Compton is a Writer at Fox News Digital. Sophia was previously a business reporter covering finance, energy and tourism and has experience as a TV news producer. She graduated with a journalism degree in 2021 from the University of Hawaii at Manoa. Story tips can be sent to sophia.compton@fox.com.

title: Army sergeant pleads guilty to cashing in on US military secrets in China-linked plot, DOJ says
summary: Sgt. Jian Zhao faces up to 10 years in prison after pleading guilty to selling national defense information from Joint Base Lewis-McChord, prosecutors say.
story: U.S. Attorney Scott Bradford announces charges against Army Sgt. Jian Zhao, accused of passing sensitive U.S. military information to individuals linked to China. (Credit: Scott Bradford, U.S. Attorney for the District of Oregon)
An active-duty U.S. Army sergeant pleaded guilty Monday in a yearslong plot that turned his access to sensitive military information into a payday from buyers in China.

Jian Zhao, 37, used his personal cellphone to photograph restricted Army documents, handed over excerpts from technical manuals for the High Mobility Artillery Rocket System, or HIMARS, and put military computers and government hard drives up for sale, federal prosecutors said.
"Protecting our national security depends on holding accountable those who compromise their oath and endanger the security of our armed forces," U.S. Attorney Scott E. Bradford wrote on X.
CHINA COULD EXPLOIT US TECHNOLOGY TO THREATEN AMERICAN FORCES, CONGRESSIONAL WATCHDOG LEADERS WARN
"Jian Zhao violated that trust by exploiting his access to military information and equipment for personal profit while knowingly providing materials to individuals linked to China."

Zhao pleaded guilty to conspiring to gather, transmit and transfer national defense information. Prosecutors said he enlisted in 2017 and served as a battery supply sergeant at Joint Base Lewis-McChord in Washington, where his duties and security clearance gave him access to sensitive Army information and equipment.
CHINA-LINKED HACKERS INFILTRATED US GOVERNMENT NETWORKS BEFORE FBI TAKEDOWN

A redacted image released by the Justice Department shows a person holding a cellphone at a desk. According to court records, Army Sgt. Jian Zhao admitted using his personal cellphone to photograph controlled military documents. (U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Oregon)
The documents Zhao photographed covered Army operations, communications networks, military exercises and rocket and missile systems, prosecutors said.
He also took military storage devices without permission and collected thousands of dollars for materials he described as sensitive, secret or top secret.
SENIOR US ARMY SOLDIER ARRESTED IN UK ON SUSPICION OF SPYING FOR RUSSIA
A U.S. Air Force C-17 sits on the flight line at Joint Base Lewis-McChord in Washington, where Army Sgt. Jian Zhao was stationed. (Smith Collection/Gado/Getty Images)

"This guilty plea reflects a deliberate betrayal of the oath every Soldier takes to defend our nation and safeguard our fellow service members," said Brig. Gen. Sean Stinchon, who leads Army Counterintelligence Command.
Stinchon said the scheme put soldiers at risk and urged troops to report suspicious activity or outreach.
CALIFORNIA REALTOR NABBED AT LAX IN ALLEGED CHINA SPY CASE TARGETING TAIWAN PRESIDENT’S RELATIVE

Prosecutors traced the plot back to late 2021. Ruoyu Duan, a former Army soldier living in Hillsboro, Oregon, recruited Zhao and other active-duty troops to provide defense information and helped arrange payments from buyers in China, prosecutors said. Duan previously pleaded guilty to conspiring to transmit national defense information.
Federal agents arrested Zhao at his home in Lacey, Washington, on March 6, 2025, and recovered about $30,000 in cash, electronic devices and multiple Army hard drives.
FORMER CALIFORNIA MAYOR ADMITS TO SECRETLY WORKING FOR CHINA, SPREADING BEIJING PROPAGANDA IN US
Two soldiers in camouflage stand in front of a tan military truck. (Christopher Chen/U.S. Air Force)
Under his plea agreement, Zhao agreed to forfeit $17,500 in proceeds from the scheme and give up his claim to the seized cash.

"By pleading guilty, Jian Zhao has admitted to betraying that trust and abusing the responsibilities that came with his position and security clearance," said Doug Olson, the FBI’s special agent in charge in Portland.

"Those who choose to compromise sensitive military information for personal gain put our nation's interests at risk, and the FBI, alongside our law enforcement and military partners, remains committed to holding them accountable," he continued.

title: Four illegal immigrants among six arrested in Florida slaughterhouse torture case, AG says
summary: Six workers at Ali Meat International, an Orlando halal slaughterhouse, face animal cruelty charges as four are held on ICE detainers, officials say.
story: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier announces six arrests in an Orlando halal slaughterhouse animal cruelty case and says ICE issued detainers for four workers. (Credit: Florida Attorney General’s Office)

Customers could buy an animal and slaughter it themselves at a public event in Orlando, where video of what happened next led to six arrests and drew a rebuke from Florida’s attorney general, who called it "pure evil."

Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier announced Monday that six workers at Ali Meat International, a halal slaughterhouse, face charges in the case. In a post on X, he singled out four workers he said were in the country illegally.

"Florida will not tolerate the abuse and torture of defenseless animals," Uthmeier wrote. "Four are illegal aliens who never should have been here, and they will be punished and sent back to where they came from."
ICE-LED FLORIDA OPERATION NETS 500 — INCLUDING ILLEGAL ALIENS ACCUSED OF MURDER, CHILD ABUSE, CARTEL TIES

Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier announces charges against six Ali Meat International workers at a Nov. 23, 2026, press conference alongside Florida Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson. (AG James Uthmeier)

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement placed detainers on those four workers, according to Uthmeier’s office. At Monday’s press conference, Uthmeier said the state would prosecute them before any deportations.

State agricultural agents arrested the six workers Friday while serving a warrant at the business. Among them was manager Nadeem Shakeel, 44, who faces up to 105 years in prison if convicted as charged, according to the attorney general’s office.
WOMAN PLEADS GUILTY TO PAYING FOR SEXUAL TORTURE VIDEOS INVOLVING MONKEYS FOR ONLINE GROUP: 'SICK PERSON'

U.S. Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins meets with federal agents in Orlando, Florida, on Nov. 20, 2026, when federal investigators joined state authorities in an operation at Ali Meat International. (@secrollins via Instagram)

U.S. Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins said federal food safety investigators reviewed video from the facility and found violations of federal humane slaughter law. She said USDA immediately revoked the facility’s permission to slaughter livestock without federal inspectors present.
Rollins said USDA’s Office of Inspector General joined Florida authorities in Friday’s operation and that she was in Orlando to thank investigators.
WARNING: GRAPHIC DETAILS
"Animal cruelty is unacceptable," Rollins wrote. "We will hold those responsible accountable."

The state opened its investigation in August 2025 after a person who saw the June event advertised on social media turned over 19 videos. In one recording, investigators say, a worker put a knife in the hand of a boy believed to be 12 or 13, then held his wrist to make him cut a sheep’s throat.
"Subjecting children firsthand to this horrific behavior is unthinkable," Uthmeier said at the press conference.
CALIFORNIA TEEN FACES PRISON AFTER VIRAL VIDEO SHOWS HIM SQUARING UP, REPEATEDLY KICKING SEA LION IN THE FACE
An exterior view of Ali Meat International, the Orlando halal slaughterhouse where Florida authorities arrested six workers in an animal cruelty investigation. (Google Maps)

Investigators said the videos showed workers carrying 16 lambs upside down by their legs, cutting their throats and tossing them into a pile. An employee walked over the lambs while several were still moving, according to Uthmeier’s office.
Investigators also said cattle were repeatedly shocked with electric prods, including in the mouth and face, and that one customer made at least 15 cuts as an animal struggled to breathe.
69 LIVE ANIMALS FOUND STUFFED IN PILLOWCASES IN HIDDEN CAR COMPARTMENT AFTER BORDER ARREST: FEDS

Nadeem Shakeel, 44, the manager of Ali Meat International, was one of six workers arrested in an animal cruelty investigation at the Orlando halal slaughterhouse. (Fox 35 Orlando/Orange County Sheriff's Office)

Assistant Statewide Prosecutor Lauryn Day said complaints about the business dated back to 2021. During Friday’s search, she said, investigators found live animals standing in mud and feces and storage areas littered with dirty socks and trash. The animals were placed in temporary care while the state works with the U.S. Department of Agriculture to arrange their transfer.
"Religious beliefs do not provide a license to disregard animal welfare laws or subject animals to unnecessary suffering," Day said.

Florida Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson said his department was investigating other animal cruelty cases and urged anyone who knows about similar practices to come forward. "We’re not going to tolerate animal cruelty here in the state of Florida," he said.

Shakeel told investigators he organized the event, oversaw staff and customers and handled the money, according to Uthmeier’s office. Agents said they found a stolen rifle in the office that Shakeel acknowledged was his. He faces a firearm theft charge in addition to animal cruelty, cattle abuse and conspiracy charges.
Another worker, Gelacio Santiz, told investigators he began slaughtering animals while they were still conscious, the office said.

The attorney general’s office identified the four workers with ICE detainers. Gelacio Santiz, 36, and Lorenzo Santis Diaz, 26, are from Mexico. Muhammad Irfan Khan, 44, is from Pakistan, and Jean Deolis, 57, is from Haiti.
VIDEO SHOWS FLORIDA FOOD TRUCK WORKERS FLEEING FROM ICE DURING TALLAHASSEE IMMIGRATION RAID
Belal Khaled Dohast, 45, was also arrested and faces animal cruelty and conspiracy charges.

All six were being held at the Orange County Jail as of Monday’s announcement. Day said each had made an initial court appearance and that their bond conditions bar them from contacting one another, having contact with animals or returning to the business.

Uthmeier said the slaughterhouse was no longer operating as of Monday and that the state was considering civil action. His office said the criminal investigation remains open and more charges are expected.

title: Fiona the hippo's tragic death prompts Cincinnati Zoo to install new safeguards at Hippo Cove
summary: New safety protections have been introduced at Hippo Cove as the Cincinnati Zoo reopens following Fiona's death, with guests urged to secure belongings.
story: Fiona, the Cincinnati Zoo's 9-year-old Nile hippo, died Thursday after ingesting a visitor's knitted hat that was inadvertently deflected into her habitat by a ceiling fan. She was born six weeks early at 29 pounds in 2017. She beat steep odds to draw millions of fans worldwide.

The Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden officially reopened its Hippo Cove exhibit on Monday, introducing new safety measures just days after the death of Fiona, the zoo’s famous 9-year-old Nile hippopotamus.

Fiona died on Thursday, Nov. 19, after swallowing a visitor’s knitted hat that was accidentally deflected into her enclosure. Zoo officials shut down the habitat "to give keepers space" following the incident, according to a Monday news release.
While Hippo Cove already met "strict" industry guidelines, zoo leaders said additional safeguards were installed before welcoming guests back.

"Even though the habitat already met strict standards set by the [Association of Zoos and Aquariums], we made some modifications to guard against something like this ever happening again," Cincinnati Zoo Director Dave Jenike said in a statement.
BELOVED HIPPO FIONA DIES AT CINCINNATI ZOO AFTER SWALLOWING VISITOR'S HAT
Fiona died on Thursday, Nov. 19, after swallowing a visitor’s knitted hat that was accidentally deflected into her enclosure. (John Minchillo/AP Photo)
"We added a layer of netting above the viewing windows and, out of an abundance of caution, removed all ceiling fans in the area."
As the exhibit reopens to the public, visitors will be able to once again see Fiona's 27-year-old mother Bibi, 23-year-old Tucker, and her 4-year-old brother Fritz.
Zoo leadership confirmed the hippos are "behaving normally" amid the loss.
"They have been getting extra care, attention, a few more pumpkins, and according to the Zoo’s director of animal care, are behaving normally," the news release noted.

Despite the upgraded barriers, zoo officials stress that they still rely on guests to secure their personal belongings, take extra care near all animal habitats, and notify staff immediately "if they see something that shouldn’t be in a habitat."
ZOO SHARES NECROPSY FINDINGS FOLLOWING FIONA THE HIPPO’S HEARTBREAKING DEATH
Despite the upgraded barriers, zoo officials stress that they still rely on guests to secure their personal belongings and take extra care near all animal habitats. (John Minchillo/AP Photo)

"The Cincinnati Zoo has been accredited since 1978 and was last accredited in 2025 after an exhaustive inspection, a standard practice for Zoos seeking or renewing accreditation," Association of Zoos and Aquariums (AZA) President Dan Ashe said in a statement.

"Nothing was of concern for the hippo habitat in the inspection report. It seems like it was a freak event that couldn’t have been foreseen. Our hearts go out to all the professionals at the Cincinnati Zoo. I know they are [devastated] by this."
Macy’s also announced via its Instagram story that it will honor Fiona during the upcoming 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade, according to People magazine.

"Fiona brought joy to millions, including so many in the Macy’s community in Cincinnati. This year, as Macy’s welcomes our own beloved Blue Hippo back to the Parade, we wanted to mark Fiona’s memory," the retailer said.
"With the Cincinnati Zoo’s blessing, Macy’s has made a donation to the zoo in Fiona’s memory and Blue Hippo’s handlers will wear a purple Fiona patch during the 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade."
EXCLUSIVE: NIH FUNDED FOREIGN LABS WITH TROUBLING SAFETY LAPSES, INCLUDING DEADLY BAT VIRUS EXPERIMENT
Macy’s also announced via its Instagram story that it will honor Fiona during the upcoming 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade. (AP Photo/Obed Lamy)
Fiona captured the hearts of people all over the country after surviving an early birth in January 2017. Born six weeks early at just 29 pounds, Fiona rapidly drew enthusiastic online followers.

Her death occurred roughly a decade after another high-profile demise at the same zoo, when Harambe, a 17-year-old western lowland gorilla, was fatally shot by zoo staff in May 2016 after a young boy climbed into his enclosure.

title: Venezuelan illegal immigrant arrested in Utah after soliciting assassination of Trump, DHS says
summary: DHS says an FBI tip led to the arrest of a Venezuelan national in Provo, Utah, over stickers urging the assassination of President Donald Trump.
story: An illegal Venezuelan immigrant was arrested in Provo, Utah, last month after investigators linked him to images encouraging President Donald Trump's assassination, the Department of Homeland Security said.

An illegal immigrant was arrested in Utah last month after an investigation linked him to the distribution of images encouraging the assassination of President Donald Trump, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) announced Monday.
Hector Alejandro Mujica-Hernandez, a Venezuelan national living in the U. S. illegally, was taken into custody in Provo.
Authorities said the arrest followed a tip from the FBI regarding online assassination threats against Trump that were traced back to Mujica-Hernandez's activity.
SECRET SERVICE ARRESTS ARMED VENEZUELAN MIGRANT NEAR WHITE HOUSE OVER ALLEGED TRUMP ASSASSINATION THREAT
Hector Alejandro Mujica-Hernandez, an illegal immigrant from Venezuela, allegedly solicited the assassination of President Donald Trump. (Department of Homeland Security)

"This illegal alien not only broke our laws by illegally overstaying his visa, but threatened the life of the President of the United States," Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin said in a statement. "The Department of Homeland Security will not tolerate death threats of any kind."

According to DHS, the investigation centered on stickers distributed during a meeting of a group called "People of Provo Against ICE" (POPAI). The stickers featured rhetoric supporting Trump's assassination, including the phrase: "Shoot Trump, be a hero, become unforgettable."
DHS noted that the letter "A" on the stickers was stylized as an upside-down anarchist symbol commonly associated with Antifa and anarchist groups.
EXCLUSIVE: DHS SECRETARY MULLIN SLAMS SANCTUARY POLITICIANS AS ATTACKS ON ICE OFFICERS SKYROCKET

Trump has been the subject of several assassination plots, while U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers have faced an uptick in attacks amid the administration's immigration enforcement agenda.
"The media and the far-left must stop vilifying ICE law enforcement officers and President Trump," said Mullin, casting blame on both for threats and attacks against ICE and Trump.

title: California nursing student and mom arrested months after man’s body turns up in ravine: police
summary: A truck driver's call near Livermore, California, led police to Marcelino Perez Jimenez's body in a ravine and a murder investigation reaching San Jose.
story: A truck driver’s roadside stop near Livermore led police to a man’s body in a ravine. A 22-year-old nursing student faces a murder charge, and her mother is accused of helping cover up the crime.
A truck driver’s roadside stop near Livermore, California, led police to a man’s body in a ravine and, eventually, to a 22-year-old nursing student and her mother.
The driver called 911 on Aug. 25 after spotting what appeared to be a body below the road, KTVU FOX 2 reported.

Alameda County sheriff’s deputies found Marcelino Perez Jimenez who had been stabbed multiple times. San Jose police say they believe he was killed in an apartment where he was last seen three days earlier.
HIKER IN GEORGIA MAKES DISTURBING DISCOVERY ON MOUNTAIN

California nursing student Alexia Nieves Solache, left, faces a murder charge in the death of Marcelino Perez Jimenez. Her mother, Veronica Rangel, is accused of helping conceal the crime. (San Jose Police Department)
Jimenez had gone into the apartment with Alexia Nieves Solache on Aug. 22. She was carrying a 24-pack of beer, according to charging documents reviewed by The Mercury News.

The next day, security cameras at the complex allegedly caught Solache and her mother, Veronica Rangel, struggling to move a heavy box. The women used a hand truck to get it into a rental car, the documents said.
WIFE AND DAUGHTER ARRESTED AFTER DNA IDS MAN WHOSE SEVERED HEAD WAS FOUND IN TRASH BAG

Booking photos of Alexia Nieves Solache, left, and Veronica Rangel are shown over a road near the ravine where Marcelino Perez Jimenez’s body was found. (County of Alameda, CA - Government Facebook/San Jose Police Department)
Police say investigators traced a vehicle from the complex to the stretch of road near the ravine where Jimenez was found.
Police arrested Solache in Los Angeles on Oct. 27 and took Rangel, 55, into custody in San Jose the same day. Both were booked on suspicion of murder, police said.
MAN ACCUSED OF KILLING PARTNER ARRESTED IN MEXICO NEARLY TWO YEARS AFTER FLEEING WITH THEIR TWO CHILDREN
San Jose police vehicles are seen behind yellow crime scene tape in a file image from an unrelated incident. (KTVU)

Solache faces a murder charge, and Rangel is accused of helping conceal the crime, The Mercury News reported. Rangel was released under supervision and told the outlet she believes her daughter acted in self-defense.

title: Anti-ICE protesters at Seattle-Tacoma airport force security presence during busy holiday travel
summary: Video captures anti-ICE demonstrators mocking a purported "bomb technician" and cursing at Seattle-Tacoma airport police during holiday travel rush.
story: Video captures demonstrators storming Seattle-Tacoma International airport, confronting police and security crews as flyers navigate busy holiday terminals. (Credit: @evanyellsatclouds via Storyful; JOHN GAEDEKE)

Video from an anti-ICE demonstrator at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport shows him taunting the police and security presence Sunday, including his mocking the sight of a purported "bomb technician."

The footage showed agitators crowding near security lines and shouting profanities at Port of Seattle police officers, whom protesters accused of acting as "collaborators." At one point in the footage, an agitator mocks the heightened security threat brought on by the demonstration.

"Let’s see what we got: Ew, bomb technician: Apparently they’re worried a bunch of dirty hippies might, I don’t know," the speaker says in the video, not completing the thought before resuming chanting and cursing at police and security officers attempting to secure the airport and help innocent travelers get through the disruptions.
DHS, DEM OFFICIALS CLASH AFTER ICE ARREST AT SEATTLE AIRPORT

The Sunday demonstrators descended on the airport during the busy holiday travel rush, after Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers detained two alleged visa overstayers on a Sea-Tac jetway Saturday morning. According to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), one was being detained before boarding a flight, prompting another woman to object and allegedly douse federal agents with hot coffee during an Alaska Airlines boarding operation.

Former Rep. Mayra Flores, R-Texas, weighed in on the controversy on X, criticizing the outrage directed at federal officers rather than the enforcement of law and order at airports during the busy travel season.
NYC ICE CHIEF FIRES BACK AT FAR-LEFT POLITICIANS SEEKING TO ABOLISH AGENCY: 'CHANGE THE LAW'

"You don’t get to come to America for a soccer game, overstay your visa for months, throw hot coffee at federal agents, and then expect the country to treat you like a victim," Flores, who was married to a U.S. Border Patrol agent, wrote. "If an American did that in another country, they’d face the consequences, not a governor rushing to their defense or headlines designed to make everyone feel sorry for them.

"ICE was doing its job: enforcing the law. The outrage shouldn’t be directed at the agents. It should be directed at the decision to overstay and assault them," Flores added. "Enforcing the law isn’t the problem. Breaking it is."
Ric Grenell, Trump administration special presidential envoy for special missions, issued a series of rebukes of the outrage and protests, noting the flouting of law and order.
DHS DENOUNCES TX OFFICIALS FOR ALLEGEDLY PLANNING TO END COOPERATION WITH ICE

"It’s the law," Grenell wrote Sunday on X, responding to Rep. Adam Smith, D-Wash., who vowed that ICE "needs to be reined in before causing more chaos and fear." "Work harder to change the law – but don’t undermine our democracy by picking and choosing WHICH laws you follow."
Grenell also expressed concern that the official Sea-Tac airport leadership was calling out ICE.
"Seems very dangerous to fly into Seattle Tacoma Airport if they refuse to enforce Federal laws," Grenell wrote. "What other laws are they picking and choosing to ignore?"
CHILD MOLESTER'S LOOMING PRISON RELEASE REIGNITES SANCTUARY SHOWDOWN IN WAKE OF DEM ELECTION SWEEP
Grenell also shared concern that a flight attendant union leader was openly breaking from supporting law and order at American airports and security checkpoints.
"Yikes. The union boss for flight attendants is calling for Federal laws to be ignored," Grenell wrote Sunday on X.
That post shared the weekend outrage from the Association of Flight Attendants-CWA President Sara Nelson.
"Get the hell out of our airports, ICE!" Taylor wrote. "@DHSgov stop your terror campaign!"
"Get OUT ICE!!!" she added in another post.
LAPD WARNS PARENTS ABOUT STUDENT SAFETY, SAYS '3RD PARTY ORGANIZERS' RECRUIT KIDS FOR ANTI-ICE WALKOUTS

The outrage and protests came after the Saturday operation around 8:05 a.m. PT as travelers boarded an Alaska Airlines flight, according to DHS. Officials stated that ICE officers targeted Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, a Mexican national accused of overstaying his visa, and subsequently arrested Sofia Hernandez Mejia after she allegedly threw hot coffee at agents interfering with the arrest. DHS stated Mejia will be charged with assaulting a federal officer.
An attorney representing Mejia disputed DHS's characterization of her client's immigration status in a statement shared with Fox News.

"She is not a U.S. citizen and was in the process of adjusting her status. It is pending with USCIS," attorney Olia Catala said. "Yes, her entry into the United States was lawful. She subsequently had pending asylum status, later married a U.S. citizen, and was undergoing the legal process to adjust her status."
The arrests sparked immediate fury from Washington state Democrats, several of whom accused federal agents of creating chaos during one of the busiest travel weeks of the year.
BUSH-APPOINTED JUDGE TORPEDOES TRUMP IMMIGRATION RULE, RIPS DHS FOR OVERSTEPPING ITS AUTHORITY

At his Saturday news conference, Democrat Washington Gov. Bob Ferguson called video of the incident "horrific" and "chilling," adding that he told Alaska Airlines representatives that "they need to call on ICE to get out of our airports." (John Gaedeke via Storyful; KOMONEWS via AP)

Washington Gov. Bob Ferguson, a Democrat, called video of the jetway arrest "horrific" and "chilling," declaring in a Saturday news conference that "ICE is completely and totally out of control." Ferguson urged Alaska Airlines representatives to "call on ICE to get out of our airports," adding he plans to make the same request to other carriers operating out of Sea-Tac.

Rep. Pramila Jayapal, D-Wash., accused the law enforcers of terrorizing the community, comparing the incident to that of "fascist states." Smith described ICE as "operating as a paramilitary force that is a profound threat to our community," while Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson called the enforcement tactics "unacceptable and un-American."

DHS pushed back against the criticism, defending the agents and pointing to what the agency described as a surge in violence against federal officers, citing DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin's directive to prosecute anyone who assaults or obstructs law enforcement to the fullest extent of the law.

"Our brave law enforcement is facing more than a 1,600% increase in assaults, 300% increase in vehicular attacks, and an 8,000% increase in death threats against them," DHS wrote on X. "This violence must end."
