It was always the goal for people to have the opportunity to watch Season 1, so that that would be an off ramp, and they could jump into Season 2. Season 2 felt like it came alive. We felt like we were a team that’d been playing together for years, instead of trying to find our feet and figuring out colors and tones. Also we just have such a wonderful crew and cast. It’s such a massive ensemble. I think everybody says that their show has the best cast and crew in the world. So somebody has to be lying somewhere. But I really stand by the fact that my cast and my crew are the best of the best.”

title: ‘Abbott Elementary’ Star Janelle James Says She ‘Bullied’ Her Way Into a Role in ‘GTA VI’: ‘Dream Come True’
summary: Janelle James of “Abbott Elementary” explains how she landed a role voicing a radio host in “Grand Theft Auto VI.”
story: If you recognize the voice of a certain radio host in the midst of committing motorized mayhem while playing “Grand Theft Auto VI,” you’re not imagining things.
Comedian and “Abbott Elementary” star Janelle James says she “bullied” her way into being included in the blockbuster video game because she is a diehard fan of the “GTA” series.

James is featured as a radio host in the game, which was released to acclaim on Nov. 19 after a 13-year wait since the last edition of “GTA.” She shared the lengths she went to in order to secure her role in a social media post.

“It’s very important to me that everybody knows that not only is that me, I’m not simply ‘voice acting,’” she wrote on her Instagram story Nov. 19. “I pursued, conceptualized, pitched, scripted AND voice acted my radio show.”
James added that she cast comedian friends Zainab Johnson and Liza Treyger on her show on the game, which was created by Rockstar Games.
“Rockstar didn’t ‘choose’ me, I bullied my way to them,” James wrote. “I’ve been playing this game since Vice City and this is a literal dream come true!!”
“Vice City” is an earlier version of the game that was released in 2002.

“GTA VI” allows players to toggle between the characters of Jason, a military veteran with a history of working with drug runners, and his girlfriend, Lucia, a fighter who was recently released from prison. The main characters are voiced by Dylan Rourke and Manni L. Perez.

Gamers had already been speculating that it was James’ voice they were hearing before she confirmed it. James, who plays principal Ava Coleman on “Abbott Elementary,” was instantly recognizable to people playing the game when it first came out.
“Janelle James from Abbott Elementary?!?!?!” one fan wrote on X with a clip from the game with James’ radio show playing.
“Janelle james in gta 6 radio just made this game 100 times better,” another wrote.
“NOT AVA BEING IN GTA 6 LMFAOOO ICONIC,” another posted.
James, 47, also responded to the outpouring of support in her post.
“I’m told the response is already great, TY,” she wrote. “Hope to catch ya’ll in these online streets where I will promptly kick you square in your back then put two in your dome. Cheers!!!”

title: Where Are Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison of ‘The Altruists’ Now?
summary: Two of the central figures involved in the collapse of the cryptocurrency exchange FTX into bankruptcy and subsequent trials for fraud have returned to the spotlight four years later.
story: Two of the central figures involved in the collapse of the cryptocurrency exchange FTX into bankruptcy and subsequent trials for fraud have returned to the spotlight four years later.

The new scripted Netflix series “The Altruists,” which begins streaming on Nov. 19, dramatizes the dynamic between Sam Bankman-Fried and his former girlfriend, Caroline Ellison, as they tried to remake the global financial system only for the company to implode in scandal.
Emmy-winning “Ozark” star Julia Garner portrays Ellison, and “Say Nothing” actor Anthony Boyle plays Bankman-Fried in the new series.
Boyle spoke on TODAY Nov. 20 about how he had “a lot of source material” about Bankman-Fried to prepare for the role because of all the interviews he did during FTX’s rise and fall.

“Because there was so much written about him, there was so many different aspects of him from different angles,” Boyle told Craig Melvin, Dylan Dreyer and Al Roker. “So some people thought he was a villain, some people thought he was the white knight of crypto, so I had a lot to draw on.”
Boyle said he also corresponded with Bankman-Fried via email from prison, where Bankman-Fried is serving a 25-year sentence.
“I was really bowled over by his intelligence,” Boyle said. “Even through emails I was like, ‘This guy is a savant.’ He’s so, so clever. Really, really interesting guy.”
Here is what to know about Bankman-Fried and Ellison, how their relationship dissolved, and where they are now.
Who Is Sam Bankman-Fried?
Bankman-Fried, 34, is the co-founder of the Bahamas-based FTX cryptocurrency exchange, which he started in 2019, as well as the crypto trading firm Alameda Research.
FTX became one of the world’s biggest cryptocurrency trading platforms and was valued at more than $30 billion at its peak before filing for bankruptcy in November 2022.

Bankman-Fried, an MIT graduate and son of Stanford professors, also was a prominent figure in the effective altruism movement, which is where the name of the Netflix series “The Altruists” comes from.

Effective altruism is a philosophical movement popular in Silicon Valley that includes the model of “earn to give,” meaning to make as much money as possible in order to give it away for the benefit of mankind, according to NBC News.

The movement is based on the premise that “people ought to do good in the most clear-sighted, ambitious, and unsentimental way possible,” according to a 2022 profile of effective altruism by The New Yorker.

Bankman-Fried ingrained those principles into Alameda Research and FTX, arguing that making large amounts of money would be beneficial because it would then be given away to help others. At one point, his net worth was estimated at $24 billion, according to NBC News.

A slogan that is used in the Netflix series is “all in, all the time,” meaning the altruistic decision is to always pursue the possibility of more money, even if it’s risky, because it can do the most good.

“I think Sam and Caroline both believed that the ends justified the means,” show-runner Graham Moore told Netflix’s Tudum. “Until the FBI showed up, and they found out there was a point at which that doesn’t work anymore.”

When FTX collapsed, Bankman-Fried’s mentor and a leader of the effective altruism movement, Will McAskill, disavowed him. He tweeted in 2022 that if Bankman-Fried “lied and misused customer funds he betrayed me, just as he betrayed his customers, his employees, his investors, & the communities he was a part of.”
Who Is Caroline Ellison?

Ellison, 32, is a Stanford graduate and Bankman-Fried’s former girlfriend and employee. She first met him when they were both working at the Wall Street firm Jane Street out of college in 2016, and she was introduced to the effective altruism movement by him.
She became a trader at Alameda Research in 2018 and then was elevated to co-CEO in 2021, according to a news release by the company.
Ellison and Bankman-Fried began dating in 2020 and broke up in 2022, Bankman-Fried testified at his trial in 2023, according to The Wall Street Journal.
“She wanted more from it than I was able to give,” he said.
What Happened to Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison?
Ellison went from being in a romantic relationship with Bankman-Fried to testifying against him during his trial in 2023.

A jury found Bankman-Fried guilty on all seven criminal counts against him in November 2023, which included being convicted of wire fraud and conspiracy to commit wire fraud against FTX customers and against Alameda Research lenders, conspiracy to commit securities fraud and conspiracy to commit commodities fraud against FTX investors, and conspiracy to commit money laundering.

Bankman-Fried, who pleaded not guilty to all the charges, was accused along with other FTX executives of making risky investments with billions of dollars stolen from customer accounts and using funds looted from the company to buy real estate in the Caribbean and make political donations.

Ellison’s lawyers said during her trial that Bankman-Fried had persuaded her to stay at Alameda by saying he loved her and the business needed her “while also perversely demonstrating that he considered her not good enough to be seen in public with him at high-profile events,” according to NBC News.

Ellison cooperated with federal investigators as they built their case against Bankman-Fried. Prosecutors said in a court filing ahead of her sentencing in September 2024 that Ellison’s testimony was “a cornerstone of the trial.”

Her lawyers wrote in the document that Bankman-Fried directed Ellison to help “steal billions” while she lived “in dread, knowing that a disastrous collapse was likely, but fearing that disentangling herself would only hasten that collapse,” according to NBC News.

In December 2022, Ellison accepted a plea deal on charges of financial fraud and conspiracy and cooperated with investigators in outlining the inner workings at FTX and Alameda Research, according to a court filing.
Where is Caroline Ellison Now?
Ellison was sentenced to two years in prison in September 2024 for conspiracy and fraud after taking the plea deal two years earlier.
She had faced a maximum sentence of about 110 years, but received two years due to her cooperation with federal investigators.
U.S. District Judge Lewis A. Kaplan also ordered her to forfeit $11 billion for her involvement in the collapse of FTX.
She began serving her sentence on Nov. 7, 2024, at a federal prison in Danbury, Connecticut, according to The Associated Press.
She did not end up serving the full two years. Ellison was released from federal custody on Jan. 21, 2026 after serving about 14 months, according to records from the Federal Bureau of Prisons.
She then quickly landed a job once she was released and returned to her effective altruism roots.

In a Substack post in September, the founder of Manifund, a philanthropic platform tied to the effective altruism movement, wrote that Ellison had joined the company in August. He wrote that she was hired “to develop our funding platform and research how to effectively direct philanthropic dollars.”
Where Is Sam Bankman-Fried Now?
After being convicted by a jury on all seven criminal counts against him in 2023, Bankman-Fried was sentenced to 25 years in prison in March 2024 for orchestrating the FTX fraud.
In addition to his prison sentence, he was ordered to pay $11 billion in forfeiture.

Bankman-Fried spoke with Tucker Carlson from Brooklyn’s Metropolitan Detention Center in New York City in March 2025, where he shared details about his then-cell block mate Sean “Diddy” Combs and his life in prison.
“It’s sort of dystopian,” Bankman-Fried said. “You know, the fortunate thing, the place I’m in, I’m not in ... I’m not in physical danger.”
In June 2026, a three-judge panel of the Manhattan-based 2nd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals denied his appeal to have his conviction overturned.
He is currently incarcerated at FCI Lompoc I, a low-security federal institution in Lompoc, California, according to the Federal Bureau of Prisons. His release date is listed as Dec. 15, 2043.

title: Beyoncé Sings ‘Irreplaceable’ in Spanish on TODAY in 2007
summary: Beyoncé performed “Irreplaceable” on TODAY in 2007, switching it up and singing it in Spanish.
story: As TODAY marks its 75th anniversary, the TODAY Archive is revisiting legendary interviews, stories that moved us and other iconic moments from our 75 years on the air. These are the segments that shaped TODAY and created a lasting legacy. Today, we look back at Beyoncé singing in Spanish on the plaza on April 2, 2007.
Beyoncé put on a show quite unlike anything fans were expecting when she performed on TODAY on April 2, 2007.

The iconic singer did a rendition of her hit “Irreplaceable,” that featured her adding lyrics from the Spanish-language version “Irreemplazable.” The song was featured in the deluxe edition of “B’Day,” which was released the day after her TODAY appearance.
“How y’all feeling this beautiful morning?” she asked at the top of the performance while perched on a stool, with a guitarist and bassist seated next to her and a band behind them.
Beyoncé Greets the Crowd and Switched Things Up
With a huge crowd surrounding her at the Plaza, the singer kicked off the track by encouraging them to sing along with her.
“I’m doing this acoustic style because I need y’all’s help. Are y’all going to sing this song with me? Y’all know what to do, right? Yeah? Here we go. Sing with me.”
She then launched into “Irreplaceable.”
“Y’all can be a little louder, right?” she said, shortly after starting the song.
She went nearly 90 seconds before she changed things up.
“So, you know what? I want to do something a little different. So I need y’all to be quiet and listen. This right here is for my Latino fans,” she said before singing in Spanish.
Translating the ‘Irreemplazable’ Lyrics
The translation for what she sang veers a little from the English lyrics of the song. Her Spanish lyrics translated to the following:
You see my love, this time I forgot you
In the closet, tucked away in a corner are your things
This is over
I swear I can’t stand you anymore
I don’t want you anymore, neither as a lover
This time you won’t win
You can leave and never come back
And if you think this time I will forgive you
You’ll see that you’ll never deceive me again
Just get out of here
An Energetic Ending and Cheers From the Crowd
She proceeded to sing about 40 seconds in Spanish before going back to English for the chorus and the remainder of the song.
After she finished, the crowd thunderously cheered.

title: ‘The Traitors: New Blood’ Finale Recap: Did the Faithfuls or the Traitors Win?
summary: Read a recap of the two-hour finale of “The Traitors: New Blood” to find out if the Faithfuls were victorious or if the Traitors deceived them and won it all.
story: Warning: Spoilers from the season finale of “The Traitors: New Blood” below…

After weeks of surprising murders and emotional banishments, “The Traitors: New Blood” has come to an end, revealing which player (or players) successfully navigated Alan Cumming’s wicked game and emerged from his castle a winner.

“The Traitors: New Blood,” the first all-civilian season of the reality competition show, wrapped on Thursday, Nov. 19, with an epic two-hour season finale that saw the remaining Faithfuls and Traitors fight for their survival. The season, which was filled with treachery, a tiny Traitor, a mega Traitor, “fruit-gate” and intense Round Table showdowns, saved some of its most thrilling moments for last as the Traitors — Katie and Shane — worked to deceive the Faithfuls one more time.

To make it to the Fire of Truth, the last stage of the game, all the players had to avoid banishment at the remaining two Round Tables, and the Faithfuls had to hope they weren’t the Traitors’ last murder victim.
But after last week’s mission gave the Faithfuls some clues about the Traitors’ identities, Katie and Shane were forced to come up with a risky strategy in the finale to protect themselves.

Did it work? Or did the remaining Faithfuls manage to outlast all the Traitors? Read on for a recap of the supersized finale and find out who joined “The Traitors”’ winner circle nearly $250,000 richer.
The Penultimate Round Table

The first part of the finale, titled “I’m Fighting Till the End,” kicks off with the players returning to the castle after the most recent mission. Clyde begins to test his theory with some of the players that Shane could be a Traitor, sharing that he heard heavy footsteps during the mission. Clyde explains why he suspects Katie is a Traitor, as well. He points out her inability to complete the puzzle in the last mission and notes that the Traitors also struggled to finish their puzzle. Before heading to the Round Table, he asks some of his fellow Faithfuls if they are willing to vote for Katie.

At the Round Table, Alan tells the players that this will be the last time they learn the identity of the player they banish. Shane opens the discussion by criticizing Jay’s strategy throughout the game, revealing that Jay shared his goal was to confuse everyone, including Faithfuls.

When Katie jumps in to make Jay look more suspicious, Clyde suggests that Jay was kept around by the Traitors to be a distraction. He says he believes Katie is a Traitor and mentions the mission puzzle as evidence. Katie admits she isn’t sure how to defend herself before Jay becomes the focus again. Victor points out that Jay voted with the banished Traitors every week and he isn’t open to accepting new information.

All the players vote to banish Jay, who casts a vote for Victor once again, and he is eliminated. On the Circle of Truth, he says, “This has been the ride of my life. I genuinely mean that. When I first came in here, I was a Faithful. But now… I am a Faithful!”
The Traitors’ Final Murder
As the players process the Round Table, Clyde continues to warn them about Katie. He cautions Victor, who confirms he has a crush on Katie, to watch out for her.

In the turret, Shane and Katie discuss their shortlist for murder, which only includes three options since the other players won shields in the previous mission. The two debate whether it is best to remove Victor, Kriste or Clyde from the game.

The final day in the castle arrives. All the players file into the breakfast room except for Clyde, the Traitors’ final casualty of the season. During a flashback, Katie explains that Clyde needed to go because he was coming for both Traitors. She and Shane also hatch a plan to pit Wyatt and Victor against each other before the last Round Table.

When Clyde walks into the confessional and sees a letter from the Traitors waiting for him, he says, “I knew it. Ugh, I’m so sad. But I still think that the Traitors could be Shane and Katie.” Before departing, he adds, “And for all of the Faithful left, don’t let this murder be in vain, ok? Go out there and do what you got to do.”
The Last Mission

For their last mission and final opportunity to add money to the prize pot, the players must locate bunkers around the castle grounds and break into them using dynamite. To do so, they have to split into two teams — one group traveling on wheels and the other via helicopter.

Abbey B. and Katie volunteer to fly high in the helicopter. After directing the group on land to the correct locations, Abbey B. and Katie have to rappel from the side of the helicopter to deliver the dynamite. Despite both having scary moments where they dangled in midair, Abbey B. and Katie complete their task and help raise the prize pot total to $246,300.
The episode ends with Alan advising the players to think about who they can trust.
The Final Round Table

Alan’s ominous words lead into the second part of the finale, fittingly titled “Who Do You Truly Trust?” While preparing for the last Round Table of the season, Victor says he is feeling good. He chats with Shane and Wyatt to confirm that they will all vote to banish Kriste. But during their talk, Victor decides to reveal to Wyatt that he was the player who secretly found a shield in Episode 9. Wyatt is visibly upset that Victor withheld this information from him. Shane says in his confessional that he can use this secret to create tension between Wyatt and Victor.
Wyatt relays his conversation with Victor to Kriste, who then passes it along to Abbey B. Both ladies start to question if Victor is trustworthy.

At the Round Table, Victor says he has been honest the entire game and he is suspicious of Kriste and Katie. Katie is shocked by Victor’s betrayal and says she feels like he has been lying to her. Kriste, meanwhile, rebuffs Victor’s claim that he has been truthful. She calls Victor a liar and a Traitor. “If y’all believe him, you get exactly what you deserve,” she tells her fellow Faithfuls.

But Kriste’s passionate plea has the opposite effect. Some players, including Abbey B., say that Kriste’s intense reaction was out of character and a possible attempt to save herself. Most of the players vote to banish Kriste, who votes for Victor. Katie also joins Kriste in voting to eliminate Victor, which confuses Shane.

Since she cannot reveal her identity, Kriste rises from the table and exits in silence. In her final confessional, she says, “I fought so hard at the end and I was hoping the guys would implode on each other, but they didn’t. It’s just been an amazing ride and it just makes me think what a gift it is to experience all these things in life. And I wouldn’t change a minute of it. I wouldn’t change a second.”
The Fire of Truth

Alan tells the players “one last battle remains”: the Fire of Truth. During their final moments to strategize with each other, Katie says she plans to eliminate Victor so she and Shane can win it all. However, Abbey B. is onto her and tells Wyatt that Katie is a Traitor. Elsewhere, Shane says he wants to finish the game with Katie but he knows the other players do not trust her.

Prior to the Fire of Truth, all the players join Alan for private chats. Shane shares that he wants to win the money so he can take care of his family. Katie explains that she needs the money for security. Victor says he thinks he has what it takes to win, but he needs the other players to trust him. Abbey B. calls the prize money a possible “blessing” that would allow her family to go on a vacation. As for Wyatt, he is more concerned about his allies. He says he doesn’t know if he can count on Victor and that the show has been the most difficult experience of his life.

Alan welcomes the players to the Fire of Truth, where the game will conclude. He explains that the game will end if either they all agree there aren’t any Traitors left or if only two players remain. For the first round, all the players vote to banish again, speculating there is still a Traitor among them. After voting, everyone chooses to eliminate Katie, who votes for Victor.

Katie cries in her confessional as she reflects on her elimination. “I know that wasn’t easy for anyone to do. And it is just a game and I have gained so much from this,” she says. “I am really shocked right now and disappointed in Shane. But I would not change a single thing about this experience other than me losing.”

For the second round, Victor and Shane vote to end the game but Wyatt and Abbey B. want to banish again. They all vote for Victor, who begrudgingly votes for Wyatt. Victor doesn’t have any hard feelings toward his former ally in his exit interview.

“That’s the game right? I got two Traitors out. That’s something I’m proud of,” Victor says in his last confessional. “I got to make some lifelong friends. But sweet, sweet Wyatt, he just couldn’t shake his suspicion of me and I respect it.”

For the third and final round, Wyatt, Abbey B. and Shane vote to end the game. Wyatt becomes emotional and prematurely celebrates their win. Abbey B. is also excited and tells Wyatt and Shane she trusts them. After Wyatt and Abbey B. confirm they are Faithfuls, Shane turns to them and reveals, “I am a Traitor.”

Shane immediately starts apologizing in between sobs. Wyatt and Abbey B. are initially stunned. She then doubles over and weeps. When Wyatt asks for an explanation, Shane says, “I started this game as a Faithful. I was given an ultimatum — either I accept or I get murdered,” adding that he made the choice after Joe was banished. Shane chokes up again before Wyatt and Abbey B. comfort and congratulate him.

In his confessional, Wyatt continues to have a positive attitude. “I really did go into that Round Table believing Shane was a Faithful. A win for the Traitors — that sucks! I am upset about that. But Shane played the perfect game. I can only give him credit,” he says.

Abbey B. is happy for Shane, too. “I am heartbroken and gutted. But you know what? I did the best I could with what I knew,” she shares. “To hear he was a Traitor, I can’t imagine how hard that was for him to look at us and say that. As bad as it hurts, I really am so happy for him. That’s a lot of money! Every single moment of this experience has been magical. So maybe I’m not leaving with the money, but maybe I still win.”

Shane is elated as he celebrates with Alan. “This is life-changing money. I can just finally feel like I’m not drowning under the water. I just feel like I’m barely making it and I can change my life now. Finally, I can actually help people. Thank you so much!” he cheers.
“I did it!” he shouts.
Outside, Shane reunites with the other finalists. Victor says he never expected Shane to be a Traitor. Katie tells Shane she will be ok as long as she gets an invite to his wedding.

After saying everyone is invited to his upcoming nuptials, Shane shares in his last confessional, “I’m so proud of myself. Starting out as a Faithful, then becoming a Traitor, it was so tough. Good things like that don’t really happen to me. This is one of the greatest moments of my life.”

title: Everything We Know About Manni L. Perez, ‘GTA 6’ Female Lead Lucia Caminos
summary: One of the buzziest aspects of the newly released “Grand Theft Auto VI” video game is its introduction of a major playable female character — the first in the “GTA” franchise, which has previously been criticized for its misogynistic content. While developer Rockstar Games has largely kept details about the long-awaited game under wraps, fans this week finally learned the identity of the voice actor behind new character Lucia Caminos.
story: One of the buzziest aspects of the newly released “Grand Theft Auto VI” video game is its introduction of a major playable female character — the first in the “GTA” franchise, which has previously been criticized for its misogynistic content.
While developer Rockstar Games has largely kept details about the long-awaited game under wraps, fans this week finally learned the identity of the voice actor behind new character Lucia Caminos.
Manni Perez, an actor, weightlifter and combat sports athlete, was revealed as the voice actor behind Lucia after she received a Game Awards nomination Nov. 17 for best performance.
Perez has so far not been a large part of the game’s promotion, however she publicly acknowledged her role in “GTA VI” on social media after the news of her nod.
Here’s what we know about Manni Perez.
Perez’s Character Lucia Is a Fugitive
Lucia, one of two characters that players can toggle between, is a a fighter who was recently released from prison and is hoping to thrive on the outside.

“More than anything, Lucia wants the good life her mom has dreamed of since their days in Liberty City — but instead of half-baked fantasies, Lucia is prepared to take matters into her own hands,” the game’s website says.

Together with her boyfriend, Jason, a military veteran who has a history of working with drug runners, Lucia embarks on a Bonnie-and-Clyde-type lifestyle to change her fortunes. However the couple gets caught up in the middle of a criminal conspiracy across the fictional state of Leonida after a robbery goes awry.
Lucia and Jason are then “forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive,” the website says.
Perez Has Made Appearances on Screen, Including in “Law & Order: SVU”
If Lucia’s voice sounds familiar to gamers, it’s likely because they’ve seen Perez before on screen.

The actor, who grew up in New York City and studied at NYU’s Tisch School of the Arts, according to IMBD, has appeared in several high-profile television series, including “Chicago P.D.,” “Blindspot” and Marvel’s “Jessica Jones.”
In a 2020 episode of “SVU,” Perez played Esperanza Morales, a  boxer who was arrested for murder after she attacked her boxing coach, who had been accused of raping a teen.
Perez, who’s a practitioner of MMA, Muay Thai and Brazilian jiu-jitsu, has also worked as a professional belly dancer.
The new game isn’t Perez’s first rodeo with the “Grand Theft Auto” franchise. She previously voiced a blackjack dealer for 2019’s “Grand Theft Auto Online.”
In an interview with the since-shuttered site Paz Magazine, Perez said that that her “biggest fear” was having to portray a “damsel in distress.”

“I’d prefer to play a character that whatever she’s going through, no matter how hard society wants to keep her down, she picks herself up, puts her big girl panties on (preferably cotton [laughs]) and keeps it moving,” she told the outlet.
Perez Has Barely Said Anything About the Game
Perez has said next to nothing about her involvement in the game. It wasn’t until the news of the Game Awards nomination that her identity was revealed.
Still, Perez hasn’t said much about the role aside from sharing a joint post Nov. 19 with the voice actor behind Jason, Dylan Rourke.

“Years witnessing the hardest working and most skilled artisans game making has to offer. We are truly honored to collaborate on this worldwide testament to human creativity, ingenuity, and sheer willpower,” the pair said in a joint Instagram post. “So much learned and so much to learn, keep fighting for what you love, stay humble. See y’all in Leonida.”

title: Two arrested over suspected burglary at royal family’s Sandringham estate
summary: Prince William and Princess Kate’s country home Anmer Hall has been broken into, police said. The Prince and Princess of Wales were not home, a source said.
story: LONDON — Two men have been arrested over a suspected burglary at the royal family’s Sandringham estate, British police said Tuesday, after a reported break-in at the country home of Prince William and Princess Kate.

Police responded to reports of “suspicious activity” at the address Monday evening, dispatching searches by police dogs, drones a helicopter. That resulted in two men being arrested on suspicion of burglary and trespassing, according to a statement from the Norfolk Constabulary, the local police authority. The property was unoccupied at the time of the incident, it added.

The Sun newspaper first reported that police were investigating a break-in at Anmer Hall, one of the residences used by the heir to the British throne and his wife, nestled in the heart of the royals’ sprawling estate.

Kensington Palace, which handles communications for William and Kate, said it would not comment publicly on security matters. A royal source told NBC News that the couple and their three children, George, Charlotte and Louis, were not there at the time.
The Waleses’ main home is Forest Lodge in Windsor, where they moved for a “fresh start” in 2025 after the death of Queen Elizabeth II and Kate’s cancer diagnosis.

Anmer Hall, a 10-bedroom country house built in the early 1800s, entered the royals’ extensive property portfolio when it was bought in 1898 by Queen Victoria’s son, who would later become King Edward VII.
It has been used by various royals over the years. And William and Kate often enjoy the residence for weekend breaks and holidays.
The incident will sharpen an ongoing debate about royal security.
William, as a “working royal,” receives 24-hour armed security. But his brother, Prince Harry, does not, having moved to California in 2020 and relinquished his regal duties.

Harry is in a protracted battle with authorities in a bid to reinstate this arrangement, which he argues is necessary due to his high-profile position and history of serving in the armed forces in Afghanistan.
This summer, Harry and his wife, Meghan, and their two children, Archie, 7, and Lilibet, 5, moved back to Britain.

In October 2024, burglars broke into the Windsor Castle estate west of London and stole a pickup truck and a quad bike from a farm building. King Charles and Queen Camilla weren’t at Windsor Castle at the time.

Three years earlier, a man armed with a crossbow was detained on the castle grounds. Jaswant Singh Chail was later sentenced to nine years in prison after admitting he had been encouraged by a chatbot to kill Elizabeth.

In 1982, intruder Michael Fagan managed to sneak into the queen’s private chambers while she was in bed. The queen spent 10 minutes chatting with the burglar before raising the alarm when he asked for a cigarette.

Hours after the break-in, William was meeting with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Tuesday on the doorstep of No. 10 Downing St., where they are expected to discuss issues such as homelessness.
Meanwhile Kate is set to feature in a 30-minute documentary, “Heal,” about her cancer diagnosis and remission. It will air on NBC on Nov. 30 at 8 p.m. ET/PT before streaming on Peacock from Dec. 1.

title: Crowd evacuated from American rapper Don Toliver’s concert after ‘unknown substance’ released
summary: MANCHESTER, England — Thousands of people attending a concert of American rapper Don Toliver were evacuated from a major British arena Sunday evening, police said, after an “unknown substance” was released into the crowd.
story: MANCHESTER, England — Thousands of people attending a concert of American rapper Don Toliver were evacuated from a major British arena Sunday evening, police said, after an “unknown substance” was released into the crowd.
About 12,000 concertgoers were evacuated by emergency workers just after 10 p.m. local time (5 p.m. ET) from Toliver’s show at the Co-op Live venue in the northern English city of Manchester.
The North West Ambulance Service declared a major incident and​ said the substance was “believed to ​be tear gas” and was understood to ⁠have been released toward the ​end of the show.

“We deployed several emergency crews, including our Hazardous Area Response Team, to support the safe assessment and treatment of people at the scene,” it said in a statement, adding that one person had been hospitalized.
“More than 80 people were assessed by our clinicians, with some reporting eye and respiratory symptoms. Decontamination was carried out as a precaution,” the ambulance service said Monday.

People in the crowd were suffering effects “from an unknown substance,” Greater Manchester police said in its latest statement Monday. “Enquiries are underway into what the substance is and what caused the incident,” police added.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
The venue, in the center of the busy city, was hosting Grammy Award-nominated R&B rapper-singer Toliver, whose real name is Caleb Zackery Toliver, as part of his Nitrous tour.
The Houston-based rapper is best known for hits “No idea” and “After Party,” and features on the soundtrack to the new “Grand Theft Auto VI” blockbuster game.

In a statement posted to Instagram, Toliver said he was “very sad” to announce that he would have to cancel his London show on Monday “due to the incident in Manchester” and would instead perform on Dec. 15.
“I Just Wanna Make Sure Everyone is Safe and the next Show goes on properly. My Heart and prayers are with with everyone that was injured last night,” he added.
Manchester was left shaken in 2017 after a bombing at a nearby venue during an Ariana Grande concert left 22 people dead and made global headlines.

“We understand the concern that this incident will have raised,” Assistant Chief Constable Steph Parker said Monday. “We will now begin to fully understand what this substance was and how this incident came about.”
“Several people were treated on site, and one has been taken to hospital at this time. Anyone who has left the event and since become unwell is advised to attend their local hospital,” Parker added.
Concertgoer Joey Howe, 22, told BBC Radio Manchester the lights came on and Toliver appeared to have been “rushed off stage.”

“I saw a lot of people streaming out and you go into this panic mode and you see a lot of people running out of the venue,” Howe said. He said people were “choking” and there was a “horrible smell” in the arena.
“It was just really distressing scenes and not something you want to see,” he added.
Another fan, Ben Stevenson, told the Manchester Evening News that he was in the standing section of the arena when he “started coughing and (my) eyes were kind of itchy.”
A spokesman for Prime Minister Andy Burnham, a former mayor of Manchester, called the incident “deeply worrying” and said the police would conduct a full investigation.
The venue, which opened in 2024, is due to host American singer Phoebe Bridgers on Thursday.

It said in a statement on X that it was “working closely with Greater Manchester Police to identify the cause and action appropriately. Our priority remains the safety and security of all visitors to Co-op Live, and we will provide more information once we have an update.”

title: Ukraine sinks Russian warship off Libya in latest expansion of the war
summary: Ukraine has taken its fight against Russia to the shores of North Africa, claiming to have sunk a warship off the coast of Libya in its latest expansion of the war.
story: Ukraine has taken its fight against Russia to the shores of North Africa, claiming to have sunk a warship off the coast of Libya in its latest expansion of the war.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Monday that Ukrainian naval drones had been used in the attack in the Mediterranean a day earlier, which came after Moscow said another of its ships was struck by drones in the Baltic Sea.
Zelenskyy shared footage of the attacks in a post on X, showing drones approaching several vessels followed by massive fireballs.
He said his forces deployed seven Ukrainian-made naval drones to sink the Russian corvette, Merkury, and hit a transport ship, the Angara, in an “exemplary Ukrainian operation.”

Later, in a separate post on the social media site, he said Ukraine responded “to Russia’s strikes the way it should be done, the way that is effective,” adding: “It is also important that without these ships in those waters, it will be harder for Russia to fuel conflicts and instability in that region as well.”
Ukraine’s Security Service, SBU, said the attacks took place near the Libyan port of Benghazi, some 1,500 miles from the established front lines of the conflict.

It said the corvette “regularly escorted enemy naval convoys” and in particular guarded the Angara cargo ship that was used to move weapons. “Both vessels were legitimate military targets for Ukraine, as they worked directly for Russia’s military capabilities,” the SBU said in a statement on Telegram.

Ukrainian uncrewed boats were delivered to a designated location and launched into the water from a so-called “mother ship,” the SBU said, reaching their targets despite “enemy’s attempts to destroy the Ukrainian drones from the air.” It said the Ka-27 multi-purpose helicopter was on board the corvette and was also sunk.
“The Defence Forces of Ukraine have once again shown that the Russian navy and its logistics have no safe routes, even far beyond the Black Sea,” the SBU added.
Ukraine noted that the ship was one of Russia’s newest, commissioned only in 2023.

Moscow has noted Zelenskyy’s “statement on this matter,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters Monday when asked about the attacks. He deferred to the Russian Defense Ministry, which was yet to comment.
It’s the latest example of Kyiv launching surprise attacks to hit back against the Kremlin.
But the weekend attack caused fallout in Libya, where local authorities expressed outrage and the United Nations called for an independent probe.

The eastern Libya-based government said Sunday that an explosion took place aboard a Russian vessel docked at the Benghazi naval base. It said the vessel was en route back to Russia and had stopped at the port to refuel and take on supplies.
A comprehensive investigation into the attack will be launched, it said, in coordination with Russian authorities.

title: Denmark accuses Russia of plotting to kill Ukrainian American rapper on its soil
summary: COPENHAGEN, Denmark — Authorities thwarted the attempted killing of a Ukrainian American citizen on Danish soil in a plot allegedly orchestrated by Russian intelligence services, the Danish prime minister’s office said Friday.
story: COPENHAGEN, Denmark — Authorities thwarted the attempted killing of a Ukrainian American citizen on Danish soil in a plot allegedly orchestrated by Russian intelligence services, the Danish prime minister’s office said Friday.

The Russian defense attaché has been expelled from Denmark in response, Danish Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen told a news conference. Two alleged members of the outlawed Danish gang “Loyal to Familia” have been arrested in connection with the attempted killing, police said.
Danish broadcaster DR, citing a court hearing, reported the men are suspected of having been recruited to assassinate ​a Ukrainian rapper ahead of a planned performance.
Police thwarted the alleged plot when they arrested ​the two men shortly before the rapper ​Kyivstoner’s Sept. 25 concert, which was later ⁠canceled.

It was unclear how police identified the two men, who ​were stopped in ​a vehicle ⁠carrying several weapons, or how the investigation expanded to include two other men ​who are not accused of participating ​in ⁠the alleged assassination plot targeting Kyivstoner.
However, all four men have been held in custody since September, according to ⁠the ​broadcaster.
It was also unclear how ​the Russian intelligence services allegedly recruited the two Danish suspects.

Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said: “It is a clear illustration of the grave security situation Denmark and Europe find ourselves in. We are facing a Russia under pressure which is acting more aggressively and is more willing to take risks.”

The Danes’ announcement came as tensions between Europe and Russia heightened again Friday. Two Russian missiles and a suspected drone came down in Poland in what its prime minister said was likely a provocation timed to coincide with European military exercises in his country for a possible postwar mission in Ukraine.
European Commission ​President Ursula von der Leyen said on Saturday the E.U. ⁠stands in full solidarity with Denmark.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
“This was an ​attack ⁠on E.U. ‌soil. And it is unacceptable. We stand in full ‌solidarity with Denmark. ‌And with all Member States targeted by Russian ⁠hybrid attacks,” she said in an X post.
European Council President António Costa said: “We will not be intimidated. Russia’s tactics and threats will not weaken the European Union’s resolve to continue supporting Ukraine.”
The Russian Embassy in Copenhagen said on Friday the accusations were not backed ‌with proof.

title: Trump calling Putin ‘my friend’ at APEC summit sparks backlash
summary: When President Donald Trump called Vladimir Putin his “friend” this week, European leaders and foreign policy experts were dismayed and alarmed.
story: Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, is wanted by the International Criminal Court on allegations of war crimes, and is accused of overseeing a yearslong campaign of election interference, sabotage and cyberattacks against the West.

So when President Donald Trump pointed to the Russian leader and declared, “He’s my friend,” at the historic Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China on Thursday, the reaction from some of America’s closest European allies was one of alarm and disbelief.
“God, protect us from such friends,” Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk posted to X shortly afterward.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

“The optics of embracing Putin and calling him a friend cause us some concern,” Poland’s foreign minister, Radosław Sikorski, told a news conference Thursday. He added that it posed the question of whom Trump considered a closer friend, Putin or Poland, and “if push came to shove, which friend would he choose?”

Their comments came hours before Poland’s defense minister, Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz, accused Russia of violating the country’s airspace overnight with three objects that were probably two missiles and a drone. Elsewhere, Estonia said it would close its road border crossings with Russia on security grounds for at least six months.

Much of the criticism of Trump’s remark has come from Poland, historically one of Washington’s closest allies in Europe but whose officials have grown increasingly wary of Trump’s dealings with Russia. The country, which borders Ukraine, Russia and Moscow’s close ally Belarus, has long been among the most outspoken European governments warning about the threat of Russian aggression. Its security strategy also relies heavily on the United States and NATO.
More broadly, the word “friend” also caused fresh alarm among other European governments, some of which are openly warning that Putin may expand his aggression beyond Ukraine and attack them, too.

Ultimately, there is widespread concern that elevating Putin alongside Trump and China’s Xi Jinping will legitimize and embolden a leader whom Western governments have sought to isolate over his record of grave human rights abuses and aggression against other countries, allegations he has routinely denied.

The joint declaration made by Trump, Putin and Xi after their meeting made no mention of Ukraine but condemned the International Criminal Court, which has issued a warrant for Putin’s arrest over the alleged unlawful deportation of Ukrainian children to Russia.

Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said it was “very incomprehensible” that Trump would meet with Putin, while German Chancellor Friedrich Merz was among those who warned against the meeting becoming a rerun of the Yalta Conference of 1945. The summit toward the end of World War II saw President Franklin D. Roosevelt, British Prime Minister Winston Churchill and Soviet leader Joseph Stalin effectively carve up occupied Germany and other parts of Europe.

Others, including British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, were more restrained. Asked whether Trump had “fallen for Putin’s charm offensive,” he replied that it was “quite the opposite” and that Trump had “talked about the horrific loss of life, including the loss of young Russian lives, and he spoke quite passionately about that subject.”
NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte also defended the principle of nuclear powers meeting to pursue diplomacy.
Burnham and Rutte were speaking at a meeting in Berlin of the “Coalition of the Willing,” a group of nearly 40 countries working to support Ukraine and provide security guarantees.
They were joined by Steve Witkoff and Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner, the U.S. envoys tasked with brokering peace between Moscow and Kyiv.

Trump called into a meeting of dozens of European leaders and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Thursday, telling the group that Putin was ready to end the war, according to five European officials briefed on the discussions. He also encouraged the Europeans to make a deal so they can stop spending money on Ukraine and spend it on their own countries, the officials said.
Kushner also mentioned the call in a post on X but said it was up to the president to reveal what he said.

“Trump wants to make a deal with Europe by his side. He’s not looking to impose anything unilaterally,” Kushner said. “Any deal we do will be in close consultation with Ukraine and with Europe. That’s something that he also asked us to come here today and reassure people in that regard.”

The White House did not immediately respond to an overnight request for comment on the criticisms about Trump’s comment about Putin. But Trump defended his description of the Russian president in an interview with Reuters, saying that “it’s nice to have people that have 4,000 nuclear weapons as a friend as opposed to an enemy.”

This is far from the first time Trump has spoken warmly about Putin, joking in 2013 about becoming his “new best friend.” Once in office, Trump said in 2018 that the pair “got on very well,” and in 2022, he described Putin’s initial moves against Ukraine as “genius” and “savvy.” In 2023 and again in 2024, Trump recounted telling Putin, “We’re friends.”
However, this week was the first time Trump made the declaration to Putin’s face, in front of television cameras at one of the most hotly anticipated meetings of recent years.

“It’s one thing to say in an interview, ‘We get on,’ as Trump has in the past; it’s quite another to see him crossing a room in the hotel in China with an effusive smile on his face and gushing about ‘my friend,’” said Jonathan Eyal, international director of the Royal United Services Institute, a London-based think tank. “It all felt very natural and very real.”

Mara Karlin, who was assistant secretary of defense for strategy, plans and capabilities under President Joe Biden, told NBC News that while Trump’s past actions on Greenland and Ukraine have provoked outcry, “referring to Putin as a ‘friend’ seems to evoke a visceral reaction because it is both entirely believable and inconceivable for any other American president to embrace a Russian leader so literally.”
The condemnation was not confined to one side of the Atlantic.

In the United States, Democrats were openly scathing. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer of New York called Trump’s words “embarrassing, despicable, and quite frankly pathetic,” while Sen. Jeanne Shaheen of New Hampshire, the top Democrat on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, described Trump’s “friend” as a “murderous war criminal.”

Sen. Mark Kelly of Arizona said: “Putin is not my friend. He’s not your friend. He’s not a friend of this country, and when the president of the United States refers to him in that way, it emboldens him.”
Republicans were more circumspect. Sen. Rick Scott of Florida called Putin a “thug” but acknowledged that Trump needed to work with him.

Bill Browder, a British American financier who spearheaded the international campaign for Russian sanctions and has become one of Putin’s most prominent critics, also described his “revulsion and disgust” at hearing Trump’s words.

“He’s a guy who’s a geopolitical menace, and he should not get any kind of respect, let alone from the American head of state,” Browder told NBC News in a telephone interview. “To be elevated to the top table with genuine superpowers is an unbelievable symbolic position to sit in.”

When asked about Trump’s comment at the end of the news conference following the “Coalition of the Willing” meeting in the German capital, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy only shrugged and walked offstage.

title: Iraqi security forces deploy in Iran-backed militia stronghold
summary: JURF AL-SAKHAR, Iraq — Iraqi security forces deployed in Jurf al-Sakhar, a stronghold of the Kataib Hezbollah armed group, on Friday under a deal that seeks to limit the reach of Iran’s most powerful Shi’ite militia ally in the country without provoking a confrontation.
story: JURF AL-SAKHAR, Iraq — Iraqi security forces deployed in Jurf al-Sakhar, a stronghold of the Kataib Hezbollah armed group, on Friday under a deal that seeks to limit the reach of Iran’s most powerful Shi’ite militia ally in the country without provoking a confrontation.

Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi this week ordered security forces to move against the heavily armed Kataib Hezbollah, which officials accused of running an oil smuggling network siphoning state-owned oil worth hundreds of millions of dollars in Jurf al-Sakhar.

The hardline Kataib Hezbollah (Battalions of the Party of God), branded a terrorist group by the United States, has rejected the smuggling accusations, which have led to arrests that prompted fears of an armed response. The group is among those that have claimed attacks on US forces in Gulf states since the start of the US-Israeli war on Iran.

A convoy of vehicles flying Iraqi flags headed into Jurf al-Sakhar on Friday and soldiers took up positions in the center after senior security officials told a press conference that government forces would protect the town.
Members of the Kataib Hezbollah group stood near their group’s flags.

“From Jurf al-Sakhar, we begin asserting state authority across all of Iraq, confronting corruption and weapons beyond state control,” Zaidi told government troops who entered the town, speaking from a military operations center in Baghdad.
“Our decision is firm: No weapons outside state authority, no weapons but Iraq‘s, no decisions but Iraq‘s, and no flag shall fly higher than the Iraqi flag.”
Under the arrangement, brokered by Shi’ite politicians, Kataib members were expected to withdraw to other parts of Iraq, a major oil producer and ally of both the US and Iran.
“God willing, things will be safe and secure with the presence of the security forces,” said resident Mohamed Ali.
Senior Iranian representative visited Baghdad, sources say

The deal will include the opening of a security headquarters in Jurf al-Sakhar on Saturday to oversee the handover. Iraq‘s energy police have begun securing an oil pipeline in Jurf al-Sakhar, the state news agency reported.

“Today is a historic moment in which the Iraqi Armed Forces prove that they are the nation’s shield, safety valve, and the guardian ensuring security stability for the Iraqi people,” Sabah al-Numan, spokesperson for the commander-in-chief of the Iraqi armed forces, told the press conference.

Reflecting the sensitivity of the situation, Iraqi Shi’ite political figures said Esmail Qaani, commander of Iran’s Revolutionary Guards’ Quds Force, arrived in Baghdad on Monday to help defuse tensions with Kataib Hezbollah.
So far, nine senior security and oil officials have been dismissed following an investigation focused on Jurf al-Sakhar in Babil province, about 50 km (30 miles) south of Baghdad.
Any direct confrontation with Iran’s heavily armed militia allies in Iraq could be risky.

After one of Zaidi’s predecessors ordered a similar crackdown on those armed groups five years ago, the prime minister’s Baghdad home was hit in a drone strike that authorities described at the time as an assassination attempt.
Refusal to disarm

US President Donald Trump has pressured Zaidi to disarm the militias that have struck US troops and facilities in Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates in solidarity with Tehran since the US and Israel launched attacks on Iran in February.
Kataib Hezbollah and other militias, all of whom report directly to Iran’s Revolutionary Guards, have refused to hand over their weapons to the state.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Founded in the aftermath of the 2003 US-led invasion of Iraq, Kataib is among the most influential members of the Islamic Resistance in Iraq, the umbrella group of hardline Shi’ite armed organisations supported by Iran.

Kataib Hezbollah quickly developed a reputation for deadly attacks against military and diplomatic targets during the US-led counterinsurgency war and sectarian conflict of the 2000s, using snipers, rockets, mortars and roadside bombs.
Wide Iranian sway in Iraq

Since the 2003 US-led invasion toppled Iran’s arch-enemy, longtime Sunni leader Saddam Hussein, Tehran has steadily expanded its influence in Iraq through close ties with heavily armed Shi’ite militias and political parties.

Iraqi security officials say the militias’ arsenals include assault rifles, machineguns, anti-tank guided missiles, mortars, precision-guided rockets, armed drones and some short-range ballistic and cruise missile capabilities.

Kataib has its own political party, called Huquq, or Rights, with five lawmakers. An Iraqi official report said the group also generates cash through businesses such as construction, housing, trade, tourism and currency exchange, though Kataib denies this and says it is dedicated to security.

Pro-Iranian militias, including Kataib, enjoy a semi-official status in Iraq, which critics say encourages them to act with impunity. A shadowy group with no announced leadership structure, Kataib Hezbollah has thousands of hardened fighters.
It forms several battalions in Iraq‘s Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), a grouping of armed factions set up in 2014 to fight Islamic State and subsequently recognized as an official security force.

Fighters receive state salaries and Kataib Hezbollah members, including some designated as terrorists by the US, hold senior positions in the PMF. While it is technically under the command of Iraq‘s prime minister as part of the PMF, the group often operates outside the chain of command.

title: Deadly Russian strikes hit 3 Kyiv bridges after Putin vows revenge for Crimea attacks
summary: Three bridges in Kyiv were hit in a Russian ballistic missile attack, officials in the Ukrainian capital said, after President Vladimir Putin vowed revenge.
story: KYIV, Ukraine — Three bridges in Kyiv were hit Friday in a massive Russian ballistic missile attack, officials in the Ukrainian capital said, hours after President Vladimir Putin vowed “painful” revenge for strikes on his prized bridge linking Crimea to Russia.

The attacks, which started in the early hours of the morning and continued well into the day, damaged the Podilsko-Voskresenskyi, Darnytskyi and Southern bridges connecting the left and right banks of the Dnipro River, which flows through the city, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said in a post on Telegram.

At least six people were killed and 15 injured in those strikes, Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi said in a separate post. Two others were killed in separate attacks across the country, which saw nine regions hit overnight, he said.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

The strikes on Kyiv forced authorities to restrict traffic on the bridges, impacting the movement across the capital. Klitschko asked residents not to drive private cars into the city “unless absolutely necessary” and suggested employers let staff work remotely.
Russia has been hitting Kyiv’s Southern and Northern bridges since early October, causing multiple closures, disrupting metro services and causing traffic jams.
But it is the first time that Russia hit three different bridges in a single night, and it has left most of the main road crossings over the Dnipro simultaneously damaged or restricted.
An NBC News team in Kyiv heard air raid sirens going off every few minutes overnight, accompanied by loud explosions.
After dawn broke on the rainy and foggy Friday morning, firefighters were seen putting out the flames from a strike on an industrial area in the capital.
It’s part of the daily reality for Kyiv’s residents after Russia escalated both the number of ballistic missiles it was firing at the capital and the frequency of attacks.
The latest strikes came hours after Putin said that Moscow would retaliate after Ukraine struck the Kerch Bridge linking Russia and Crimea for a third time this week.

title: Palestinians flee as Israeli tanks cross Gaza ceasefire’s ‘yellow line’
summary: Israel’s ground operation across the yellow ceasefire line in Gaza, which forced Palestinians to flee their makeshift shelters, marks a fresh escalation in the conflict and risks undermining an already floundering truce with Hamas, analysts said Thursday.
story: Israel’s ground operation across the yellow ceasefire line in Gaza, which forced Palestinians to flee their makeshift shelters, marks a fresh escalation in the conflict and risks undermining an already floundering truce with Hamas, analysts said Thursday.

As tanks rolled into central Gaza on Wednesday, residents could be seen carrying blankets and other belongings away from their tents in pictures and video taken shortly after the Israeli military began what it said was an operation targeting a “terror tunnel.”

Others could be seen rolling away mattresses on carts and pushing loved ones in wheelchairs away from the scene near the Nuseirat camp in central Gaza. At least one person was reported to have been killed in an Israeli airstrike near the raid, Palestinian medics said, according to Reuters.

“Bullets were fired at us,” Amna al-Gasar, 49, told NBC News after she fled the scene with her young children, her baby in a pink fluffy sweater strapped to her chest. She said her family had received “evacuation orders” from the Israeli military and that tanks had advanced on the area.

“This is the 14th time that we’re getting displaced,” al-Gasar said, who added that she is from Gaza City in the north of the enclave which is now on the side of the “yellow line” occupied by Israeli forces. “Where should we go? We are exhausted. This is not a life,” she said.

Muna Abu Shehadeh, 37, said in a separate interview that along with some of her relatives, she left “with nothing but our children — no bedding, no food, and no water.” She added that she had a daughter who was ill, as well as a baby, and that they had to leave behind what few supplies they had.

The Israeli military told NBC News the ground operation was the first to be executed beyond the yellow line — the boundary marking the roughly 60% of Gaza that remains occupied by Israeli forces — since the U.S.-brokered ceasefire with Hamas came into effect in October 2025.

Separately, in a joint statement with the Israel Security Agency, or Shin Bet, the Israel Defense Forces said the operation was a “targeted” assault aimed at dismantling a tunnel that “posed an immediate and direct threat” to troops.

title: Trump pushes for three-way nuclear deal as Russia and China show little interest
summary: President Donald Trump has repeatedly placed nonproliferation near the top of the agenda for his unprecedented trilateral meeting Thursday with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, but his counterparts have expressed little interest in committing to new limitations on their nuclear arsenals.
story: WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump has repeatedly placed nonproliferation near the top of the agenda for his trilateral meeting Thursday with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, although his counterparts have expressed little interest in committing to new limitations on their nuclear arsenals.

Trump has been pushing for China to join the U.S. and Russia in a new nuclear arms control agreement since his first term in office. Still, he has sought to limit expectations for any major progress in Shenzhen, China, where the world’s top three nuclear powers are meeting on the sidelines of a summit of Asia-Pacific leaders.

Russia suspended its participation in New START, its last remaining nuclear arms pact with the U.S., when it invaded Ukraine in 2022, denying inspections of its nuclear sites. Ahead of the treaty’s expiration this past February, Russia said it would keep to the deal’s limitations on its arsenal for another year, but Trump insisted a new agreement must include China and possibly other nuclear powers.

China has said an arms control agreement should remain between the U.S. and Russia, which together hold nearly 90% of the world’s nuclear arsenal, with more than 5,000 warheads each. China has about 600, according to Pentagon estimates, though by 2030 it could have up to 1,000 if its arsenal continues to expand at the current rate.

“China is building up its nuclear arsenal to a very significant degree, and it will continue to do so, and wants to continue to do so,” David Sacks, a senior fellow for Asia studies at the Council on Foreign Relations, told reporters Wednesday.

The Chinese foreign ministry has declined to say whether nuclear arms control will be discussed at the trilateral meeting on Thursday, with spokesperson Mao Ning saying earlier this week that the three leaders “will have an in-depth exchange of views on important issues bearing on global peace.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

In a call last week, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi “agreed on the importance of meaningful leader-level conversations to advance goals such as peace and denuclearization,” according to a U.S. readout of the call. The Chinese readout made no reference to such a discussion.
Trump has admitted that it will be difficult to get Russia and China to consider reducing their nuclear arsenals.

“So we’re going to talk about denuclearization. Tough subject because it’s very hard for any of us to say we’ll get rid of our nukes, right? But especially since you do have other countries,” he said Monday. “But we’re going to be talking about denuclearization.”

Even in the hours leading up to this week’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, the world’s top two nuclear powers were making shows of force. On Tuesday, the U.S. launched an unarmed intercontinental ballistic missile in a previously unannounced test at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California. Hours later, Russia landed two strategic bombers in Vietnam to coincide with Putin’s arrival in China.

While one meeting is not likely to produce dramatic breakthroughs, it could kick-start a process that leads to sustained, formal bilateral or multilateral negotiations on nuclear risk reduction, arms control and disarmament, said Daryl Kimball, executive director of the Washington-based Arms Control Association.

“A top priority for all three leaders should be to head off a costly, escalatory nuclear arms race involving the further buildup of nuclear forces and the resumption of nuclear testing by any state,” he said.

Da Wei, director of the Center for International Security and Strategy at Tsinghua University in Beijing, said nuclear arms control was not a “proper topic” for the trilateral meeting given the complexity of the issue and how little time Trump, Putin and Xi will have together.
But if the three leaders “can say something about nuclear stability, like a nuclear war is not winnable and should not be fought, I think that will be helpful,” he said in an interview Wednesday.
Rubio has acknowledged that a new agreement could take some time.

“Past agreements, including New START, took years to negotiate and were built upon decades of precedent. They were also between two powers, not three or more,” he wrote on Substack in February. “However, just because something is hard does not mean we should not pursue it or settle for less.”
